source_text: Ἐπεὶ γὰρ ἀνόμως μεθ᾽ ἡμέρας πάλιν στρεβλοῦντες τὸν μάρτυρα καὶ νομίζοντες ὅτι οἰδούντων καὶ φλεγμαινόντων τῶν σωμάτων εἰ τὰ αὐτὰ προσενέχοιεν κολαστήρια, περιέσοιντο αὐτοῦ, ὁπότε οὐδὲ τὴν ἀπὸ τῶν χειρῶν ἁφὴν ἠνείχετο, ἢ ὅτε ἐναποθανὼν ταῖς βασάνοις φόβον ἐμποιήσειεν τοῖς λοιποῖς, οὐ μόνον οὐδὲν περὶ αὐτὸν τοιοῦτο συνέβη, ἀλλὰ καὶ παρὰ πᾶσαν δόξαν ἀνθρώπων ἀνέστη καὶ ἀνωρθώθη τὸ σωμάτιον ἐν ταῖς μετέπειτα βασάνοις, καὶ τὴν ἰδέαν ἀπέλαβεν τὴν προτέραν καὶ τὴν χρῆσιν τῶν μελῶν, ὥστε μὴ κόλασιν, ἀλλ᾽ ἴασιν διὰ τῆς χάριτος τοῦ Χριστοῦ τὴν δευτέραν στρέβλωσιν αὐτῷ γενέσθαι. Καὶ Βιβλίδα δέ, μίαν τῶν ἠρνημένων, ἤδη δοκῶν ὁ διάβολος καταπεπωκέναι, θελήσας δὲ καὶ διὰ βλασφημίας κατακρῖναι, ἦγεν ἐπὶ κόλασιν, ἀναγκάζων εἰπεῖν τὰ ἄθεα περὶ ἡμῶν, ὡς εὔθραυστον ἤδη καὶ ἄνανδρον· ἡ δὲ ἐν τῇ στρεβλώσει ἀνένηψεν καὶ ὡς ἂν εἴπειν ἐκ βαθέος ὕπνου ἀνεγρηγόρησεν, ὑπομνησθεῖσα διὰ τῆς προσκαίρου τιμωρίας τὴν αἰώνιον ἐν γεέννῃ κόλασιν, καὶ ἐξ ἐναντίας ἀντεῖπεν τοῖς βλασφήμοις, φήσασα· Πῶς ἂν παιδία φάγοιεν οἱ τοιοῦτοι, οἷς μηδὲ ἀλόγων ζῴων αἷμα φαγεῖν ἐξόν; Καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦδε Χριστιανὴν ἑαυτὴν ὡμολόγει καὶ τῷ κλήρῳ τῶν μαρτύρων προσετέθη.
thought_title: Sanctus healed for a second torture and Biblis confesses
orientation: Sanctus has endured torture answering only that he is a Christian, and Biblis is one of those who first denied the faith.
pass_a_gloss: For since after days they were again twisting the martyr unlawfully and supposing that, with the bodies swollen and inflamed, if they applied the same torture instruments they would get the better of him, either when he could not even bear the touch from their hands, or when, dying under the tortures, he would put fear into the rest, not only did nothing such happen concerning him, but also beyond all expectation of men the little body stood up and was raised upright in the later tortures, and it received back its former appearance and the use of its limbs, so that through the grace of Christ the second twisting became for him not torture but healing. And as for Biblis also, one of those who had denied the faith, whom the devil thought he had already swallowed down, and wishing also to condemn her through blasphemy, he led her to torture, compelling her to say the godless things concerning us, as already fragile and unmanly; but she in the twisting came to herself and, as one might say, awoke out of deep sleep, having been reminded through the temporary punishment of the eternal torture in Gehenna, and on the contrary she answered back to the blasphemers, saying: How would such people eat children, to whom it is not even permitted to eat blood of irrational animals? And from that point she professed herself a Christian and was added to the lot of the martyrs.

choices.why: diminutive marks the emaciated tortured body, not a neutral body

choices.term: μὴ κόλασιν, ἀλλ᾽ ἴασιν ... τὴν δευτέραν στρέβλωσιν
choices.english: the second twisting became not torture but healing
choices.why: keeps the act (twisting) distinct from its effect (torture versus healing)

choices.term: Πῶς ἂν παιδία φάγοιεν οἱ τοιοῦτοι, οἷς μηδὲ ἀλόγων ζῴων αἷμα φαγεῖν ἐξόν;
choices.english: How would such people eat children, to whom it is not even permitted to eat blood of irrational animals?
choices.why: οἷς has the same referent as οἱ τοιοῦτοι, namely the accused Christians, whose blood prohibition she invokes against the slander concerning us
rejected: how would you eat children, to whom it is not permitted

choices.why: κλῆρος is an allotted portion or group, with glossary martyrs

bible_refs.note: τὴν αἰώνιον ... κόλασιν matches eternal punishment

pass_b_english: After some days they unlawfully put the martyr on the rack again. They supposed his body was swollen and inflamed, so the same instruments of torture would now get the better of him. He could not even bear the touch of a hand. Or, if he died under the tortures, fear would take hold of the rest. Nothing of that kind happened to him. Beyond all human expectation, his little body rose and stood upright under the tortures that followed, and it recovered its former appearance and the use of its limbs, so that by the grace of Christ the second twisting became for him not torture but healing.

The devil thought he had already swallowed Biblis, one of those who denied the faith, and he wanted to condemn her too through slander. So he had her led away to torture, to force her, fragile and cowed as she already seemed, to say godless things about us. But on the rack she came to herself and woke as if from a deep sleep. The passing punishment reminded her of the eternal torture in Gehenna (Matthew 25:46). So she answered the blasphemers back, saying, "How could people like that eat children, when they are not even allowed to eat the blood of brute beasts?" From that moment she professed herself a Christian and was added to the lot of the martyrs.
